description: Lamb Ouzi Whole Slow Roasted is a magnificent Middle Eastern dish featuring a whole lamb leg or shoulder, slow-cooked until incredibly tender and falling off the bone. Infused with aromatic spices, this celebratory meal is typically served over a bed of fragrant rice, garnished with toasted nuts, and is a true centerpiece for any special occasion.

instructions.title: Prepare the Lamb and Marinade
instructions.text: Pat the lamb dry with paper towels. In a small bowl, combine 1 tbsp olive oil, baharat, cinnamon, cardamom, salt, and black pepper. Rub this spice mixture generously all over the lamb, ensuring it gets into any crevices. For best flavor, cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or preferably overnight.

instructions.title: Sear the Lamb
instructions.text: Preheat a large, oven-safe Dutch oven or roasting pan over medium-high heat. Add 2 tbsp olive oil. Once hot, sear the lamb on all sides until nicely browned, about 3-4 minutes per side. Remove the lamb from the pot and set aside.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics and Deglaze
instructions.text: In the same pot, add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil. Add the chopped onions and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. Pour in about 1 cup of broth to deglaze the pot, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.

instructions.title: Slow Roast the Lamb
instructions.text: Return the seared lamb to the pot. Add the remaining broth and bay leaves. The liquid should come about halfway up the lamb. Bring to a simmer, then cover the pot tightly and transfer it to a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F). Roast for 3 to 3.5 hours, or until the lamb is fork-tender and easily pulls away from the bone.

instructions.title: Prepare the Ouzi Rice
instructions.text: About 30 minutes before the lamb is done, prepare the rice. In a separate pot, add 2 cups rinsed basmati rice with 3 cups water or broth, a pinch of salt, and a dash of cinnamon if desired. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is fluffy. Let it rest for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.

instructions.title: Assemble and Serve
instructions.text: Carefully remove the lamb from the pot and let it rest for 10-15 minutes. Shred or carve the lamb from the bone. Discard bay leaves from the cooking liquid; skim off any excess fat and reserve the flavorful pan juices. On a large serving platter, spread the fluffy rice. Arrange the shredded lamb over the rice. Drizzle with some of the pan juices, then garnish generously with toasted pine nuts, slivered almonds, and fresh chopped parsley or mint. Serve immediately.

tips: For truly authentic flavor, ensure your baharat spice blend is fresh. You can also make your own blend with cumin, coriander, cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg, cardamom, and black pepper.
Browning the lamb before slow roasting is crucial for developing a deep, rich flavor and a beautiful crust. Do not skip this step.
Serve Lamb Ouzi with a side of plain yogurt, a simple cucumber and tomato salad, or a fresh green salad to balance the richness of the dish.
article:
**Experience the Grandeur of Middle Eastern Feasts: Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi**

Imagine a dish so magnificent, so steeped in tradition and flavor, that it effortlessly becomes the centerpiece of any celebration. That dish is Lamb Ouzi, a jewel of Middle Eastern cuisine, renowned for its tender, falling-off-the-bone lamb, aromatic spiced rice, and a medley of crunchy nuts. While often associated with grand banquets and special occasions, mastering a whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi is a truly rewarding endeavor that brings the heart and soul of the Levant into your home kitchen. Prepare to embark on a culinary journey that promises an unforgettable dining experience, showcasing the rich tapestry of flavors found in this iconic Middle Eastern dinner recipe.

## What is Lamb Ouzi?

Lamb Ouzi, also spelled as Ghuzi or Ghoozi, is a traditional Middle Eastern dish that typically features slow-cooked lamb served over a bed of fragrant rice, often studded with nuts, peas, and various spices. While regional variations exist, the essence remains the same: a celebratory dish symbolizing hospitality and abundance. The "whole" aspect in our recipe refers to a substantial cut of lamb, such as a whole leg or shoulder, rather than small chops or cubes, allowing for a magnificent presentation and incredibly succulent meat. The slow roasting method is crucial here, transforming a robust cut of lamb into a melt-in-your-mouth delicacy. It’s a dish that demands time and patience but rewards with unparalleled depth of flavor, making it perfect for feeding a crowd during holidays, family gatherings, or any event deserving of an epic meal.

## Ingredients for Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi

To create this show-stopping Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi, you’ll need a combination of fresh, high-quality ingredients and a pantry stocked with Middle Eastern staples.

**For the Lamb:**
*   1 whole lamb leg (5-7 lbs / 2.3-3.2 kg), bone-in preferred
*   1 cup plain full-fat yogurt
*   1/4 cup olive oil
*   4-5 cloves garlic, minced
*   2 tablespoons Baharat spice blend (or a mix of allspice, cinnamon, nutmeg, black pepper, cardamom)
*   1 tablespoon ground cumin
*   1 tablespoon ground coriander
*   1 teaspoon turmeric
*   Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
*   2 large onions, quartered
*   4-5 bay leaves
*   4-5 cups lamb or beef broth

**For the Aromatic Rice Stuffing/Bed:**
*   3 cups Basmati rice, rinsed until water runs clear
*   1/4 cup olive oil or ghee
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   2 cloves garlic, minced
*   1 cup frozen peas
*   1/2 cup toasted slivered almonds
*   1/2 cup toasted pine nuts
*   1 tablespoon Baharat spice blend
*   1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
*   1/2 teaspoon ground cardamom
*   Salt and pepper to taste
*   4 cups lamb or chicken broth

**For Garnish:**
*   Fresh parsley or mint, chopped
*   Additional toasted nuts (almonds, pine nuts, pistachios)

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Lamb Ouzi

Crafting this Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi is a process, but each step is straightforward and contributes to the final, spectacular result.

1.  **Prepare the Lamb Marinade:** In a large bowl, whisk together the yogurt, olive oil, minced garlic, Baharat, cumin, coriander, turmeric, salt, and pepper.
2.  **Marinate the Lamb:** Pat the lamb leg dry. Using a sharp knife, make several deep slits all over the lamb. Rub the marinade generously over the entire lamb leg, ensuring it penetrates the slits. Place the lamb in a large roasting pan, cover, and refrigerate for at least 6 hours, or ideally overnight, allowing the flavors to meld and tenderize the meat.
3.  **Preheat Oven and Prepare for Roasting:** Preheat your oven to 325°F (160°C). Remove the lamb from the refrigerator at least an hour before roasting to bring it closer to room temperature. Add the quartered onions and bay leaves to the roasting pan around the lamb. Pour 2 cups of the lamb broth into the bottom of the pan.
4.  **Slow Roast the Lamb:** Cover the roasting pan tightly with foil or a lid. Roast for 3-4 hours, or until the lamb is incredibly tender and easily pulls away from the bone. During the last hour, remove the foil to allow the lamb to brown and crisp up slightly. Baste periodically with the pan juices. If the pan dries out, add more broth as needed. The internal temperature should reach 190-205°F (88-96°C) for fall-apart tenderness. This extended cooking time is key to achieving truly succulent Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi.
5.  **Rest the Lamb:** Once cooked, remove the lamb from the oven, transfer it to a carving board, and tent loosely with foil. Let it rest for at least 20-30 minutes. This allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring a moist and flavorful result.
6.  **Prepare the Aromatic Rice:** While the lamb rests, prepare the rice. In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat olive oil or ghee over medium heat. Sauté the chopped onion until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. Stir in the rinsed Basmati rice, Baharat, cinnamon, cardamom, salt, and pepper. Toast the rice and spices for 2-3 minutes.
7.  **Cook the Rice:** Pour in the 4 cups of broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until all the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.
8.  **Finish the Rice:** Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork, then gently fold in the frozen peas, toasted slivered almonds, and pine nuts.
9.  **Assemble and Serve:** To serve, create a generous bed of the aromatic rice on a large serving platter. Carefully place the whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi on top of the rice. Garnish generously with fresh parsley or mint and additional toasted nuts. Carve the lamb at the table or shred it before plating for easier serving.

## Pro Tips for the Best Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi

Achieving the perfect Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi goes beyond just following the steps. Here are some expert tips to elevate your dish:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The longer the lamb marinates, the more tender and flavorful it will become. Overnight is highly recommended.
*   **Low and Slow:** The "slow roasted" part of the name is critical. Cooking at a lower temperature for an extended period breaks down tough connective tissues, resulting in incredibly tender meat that literally falls off the bone.
*   **Rest Your Meat:** Always rest the lamb after roasting. This crucial step allows the meat fibers to relax and reabsorb the juices, ensuring a succulent and moist cut.
*   **Don't Waste Pan Juices:** The drippings in the roasting pan are liquid gold. Skim off excess fat and use the remaining jus to drizzle over the lamb and rice for an extra layer of flavor. You can also thicken it slightly for a gravy.
*   **Toasting Nuts:** Toasting the nuts for the rice (and garnish) brings out their natural oils and enhances their flavor and crunch significantly. Do this gently to avoid burning.
*   **Quality Spices:** Use fresh, high-quality spices. They make a noticeable difference in the overall aroma and taste of your Ouzi.

## Serving Suggestions for Lamb Ouzi

Lamb Ouzi is a complete meal in itself, but it truly shines when accompanied by a few refreshing sides that cut through its richness.

*   **Yogurt Sauce:** A simple plain yogurt sauce, perhaps with a touch of garlic and mint, provides a cooling contrast.
*   **Fresh Salads:** Crisp, tangy salads like Fattoush (bread salad) or Tabbouleh (parsley and bulgur salad) offer a vibrant counterpoint to the hearty lamb.
*   **Pickles:** Assorted Middle Eastern pickles (torshi) add a delightful sour crunch.
*   **Fresh Herbs:** A platter of fresh mint, parsley, and spring onions allows guests to add extra freshness to their individual plates.
*   **Warm Pita Bread:** Perfect for scooping up any leftover rice and juices.

## Variations and Substitutions for Lamb Ouzi

While the traditional Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi is a masterpiece, you can adapt it to suit your preferences or dietary needs:

*   **Lamb Cut:** If a whole leg is too much, a large lamb shoulder (bone-in) works beautifully with the same slow roasting method. For smaller gatherings, lamb shanks can also be adapted.
*   **Rice Additions:** Feel free to add other vegetables to the rice, such as carrots, green beans, or chickpeas. Some variations include vermicelli noodles toasted with the rice.
*   **Spice Blends:** Experiment with different spice blends. While Baharat is traditional, Ras el Hanout or even a simple blend of cumin, coriander, and paprika can be used.
*   **Nut Varieties:** Beyond almonds and pine nuts, pistachios, cashews, or even walnuts can be used for garnish or mixed into the rice.
*   **Vegetarian Ouzi:** For a meat-free alternative, you can create a "vegetarian ouzi" by focusing on a richly spiced rice pilaf, perhaps incorporating lentils, chickpeas, or roasted vegetables as the main protein element, served with all the traditional garnishes.

Indulging in a Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi is more than just a meal; it's an experience. It's a celebration of rich flavors, family, and the timeless art of slow cooking. This Middle Eastern classic, with its tender lamb and aromatic rice, is guaranteed to leave a lasting impression and become a cherished part of your culinary repertoire. Don't be intimidated by its grandeur; with patience and love, you too can bring this magnificent feast to your table.
